3773: /* Remove a rule from the retained command rules. Always match rules
3774:  * verbatim, but also remove subcommand rules if we are adding or removing the 
3775:  * entire command. */
3776: void ACLSelectorRemoveCommandRule(aclSelector *selector, sds new_rule) {
3777:     size_t new_len = sdslen(new_rule);
3778:     char *existing_rule = selector->command_rules;
3779: 
3780:     /* Loop over the existing rules, trying to find a rule that "matches"
3781:      * the new rule. If we find a match, then remove the command from the string by
3782:      * copying the later rules over it. */
3783:     while(existing_rule[0]) {
3784:         /* The first character of the rule is +/-, which we don't need to compare. */
3785:         char *copy_position = existing_rule;
3786:         existing_rule += 1;
3787: 
3788:         /* Assume a trailing space after a command is part of the command, like '+get ', so trim it
3789:          * as well if the command is removed. */
3790:         char *rule_end = strchr(existing_rule, ' ');
3791:         if (!rule_end) {
3792:             /* This is the last rule, so it it to the end of the string. */
3793:             rule_end = existing_rule + strlen(existing_rule);
3794: 
3795:             /* This approach can leave a trailing space if the last rule is removed,
3796:              * but only if it's not the first rule, so handle that case. */
3797:             if (copy_position != selector->command_rules) copy_position -= 1;
3798:         }
3799:         char *copy_end = rule_end;
3800:         if (*copy_end == ' ') copy_end++;
3801: 
3802:         /* Exact match or the rule we are comparing is a subcommand denoted by '|' */
3803:         size_t existing_len = rule_end - existing_rule;
3804:         if (!memcmp(existing_rule, new_rule, min(existing_len, new_len))) {
3805:             if ((existing_len == new_len) || (existing_len > new_len && (existing_rule[new_len]) == '|')) {
3806:                 /* Copy the remaining rules starting at the next rule to replace the rule to be
3807:                  * deleted, including the terminating NULL character. */
3808:                 memmove(copy_position, copy_end, strlen(copy_end) + 1);
3809:             }
3810:         }
3811:         existing_rule = copy_end;
3812:     }
3813: 
3814:     /* There is now extra padding at the end of the rules, so clean that up. */
3815:     sdsupdatelen(selector->command_rules);
3816:     ACLSelectorCaptureRuleDigest(selector, NULL, NULL, ACL_OK);
3817:     ACLSelectorSummarizeRuleDigest(selector, NULL, NULL);
3818: }

part.text: All ACL tests pass. Cleaning up the temporary repro files:

Fixed the bug in `ACLSelectorRemoveCommandRule` (src/acl.c:3808).

**Root cause:** When removing a matched rule via `memmove`, the loop advanced `existing_rule` to `copy_end`, but the shift left by the removal means `copy_end` points into the middle of the following rule in the new string — so the following rule got partially skipped and never matched/removed.

**Fix:** After a removal, restart the loop at `copy_position` (where the next rule now begins), and only advance to `copy_end` when no rule was removed.

**Verified:**
- Issue repro `+config|get -config|set` + `+config` now yields `resetchannels -@all +config` (matches ACL LIST and actual permissions, `CONFIG SET` is allowed)
- `./runtest --single unit/acl` — all tests pass (including the previously failing `ACL SETUSER ... +config +config|get -config|set +config` → `-@all +config` case)
